title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026

Reason for Admission: Abdominal pain and vomiting.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 76, Temp 98.6 F, SpO2 98% on RA, RR 16.

Recent Labs: WBC 11.2, Hgb 14.1, Plt 210, Na 138, K 4.1, Cl 101, HCO3 23, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, Glucose 105.

Social History: Lives with spouse, non-smoker, occasional alcohol use.
Family History: Father had hypertension, Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight loss.
Eyes: Normal vision.
ENT: No sore throat or rhinorrhea.
Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations.
Respiratory: No shortness of breath or cough.
Gastrointestinal: Positive for abdominal pain and nausea.
Genitourinary: No dysuria.
Musculoskeletal: No joint pain.
Neurological: No headaches or dizziness.

History of Present Illness (Copied Forward): Patient is a 51-year-old male presenting with sudden onset of severe mid-abdominal pain. He reports associated nausea and several episodes of non-bilious vomiting over the last 12 hours. He denies any recent changes in bowel habits.

Hospital Course: The patient was admitted for evaluation of acute abdominal symptoms. Imaging and clinical assessment revealed a partial small bowel obstruction. The underlying etiology of the obstruction was not identified during the course of the stay. Management was initiated with intravenous fluids and bowel rest. The patient tolerated the bowel rest well, with a significant decrease in pain and resolution of vomiting. Serial abdominal exams showed improving bowel sounds and decreased tenderness. The obstruction resolved without the need for surgical intervention. The patient was transitioned to a clear liquid diet and eventually tolerated solid foods before discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Partial small bowel obstruction, unspecified cause.

Discharge Medications:
1. Ondansetron 4mg as needed for nausea.
2. Acetaminophen 650mg as needed for pain.

Follow-up: Patient instructed to follow up with primary care physician in 1 week for a routine check-up. Patient advised to return to the emergency department immediately if he experiences worsening pain, persistent vomiting, or fever.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD, 05/15/2026
explanations: Partial intestinal obstruction, cause not stated: K56.600 (HCC 78).
